title: The Infinitely Deep Shelf Where Books Choose Their Companions

features.name: the organizing spiral
features.desc-on-touch: books turn in layers around a centre nothing, each one chosen by resemblance rather than system. you trace a spine and find six others it touches without touching.

features.name: dust in organizational light
features.desc-on-touch: motes drift through a shaft where meaning has become visible. you can almost read what the archive is thinking by watching where they fall.

features.name: the filing glyph
features.desc-on-touch: a plaque whose characters rearrange themselves each time you look away. the archive is rewriting its own index.

features.name: the trunk of concatenations
features.desc-on-touch: a eucalyptus growing sideways, its rings marked with cross-references. the wood is both shelf and ledger.

features.name: the cascade where copies return to originals
features.desc-on-touch: water that holds reflected books, each reflection a different filing system, all trying to claim the centre.

inscription: here the books have stopped pretending they need the system; they choose each other by the only method the archive ever believed in: resemblance that echoes back

reverie.title: REVERIE — the library where hands first saw resemblance
narr: dust motes catch on what she holds up to the light,
and you see suddenly how the binding and the photo
from three files back have the same rust-stain colour.
neither of you planned it that way. the archive is
making connections you were too literal to make.
she sets them spine-to-spine. they belong together now.
